description.narrative: Stöd till MEM med capacitet höjande projekt för planering och management av energi sektor i Tanzania
Support to MEM capacity for planning and management of the energy sector in Tanzania

The main objective of the support is increased access to modern energy services through enhanced availability, reliability and affordability of energy supplies that are friendly to the environment. It is MEMs role to manage the energy sector through policy design, legislation and regulation supported by channeling of public financial resources to achieve that objective for the benefit of all Tanzanians. The project is a capacity building project that will support Ministry of Energy to better manage the energy sector.
For the Ministry of Energy (MoE) to have quality and reliable data and information, an Energy Information Management System (EIMS) is required. A strong Energy Information Management System requires institutional coordination among different parties in the energy sector as well as proper funding for a sustained capacity building of skilled people with relevant statistical and analytical tools to create and correlate the data at national level.
The main objective of Sida is to assist the Ministry of Energy (MoE) to create an elaborative energy information management system for all types of energy produced and consumed in Tanzania and to harmonize the data available in the region. This should be able to facilitate rapid transfer and exchange of information among regional countries. The Energy Information Management System is expected to be a bedrock of preparation of periodic National Energy Balances; Energy Demand Forecasting as well as Energy Supply Forecasting.

description.narrative:
The MoE secured approvals from eGovernment Authority, Public Service Commission and Good Governance, and Chief Secretary on 30th January 2023, then initiated process for procurement of consultant for preparation of National Energy Information Management System (NEIMS). Through competitive procurement process, ICTPack Solutions Ltd., was recruited on 28th November 2024 to support the Ministry in undertaking the development of the National Energy Information Management System (NEIMS), a digital platform designed to centralize, harmonize, and manage energy data from across the energy sector in Tanzania. The system aims to improve energy planning, policymaking, and reporting by ensuring the availability of accurate, timely, and disaggregated data on energy sources and consumption patterns.
The narrative report indicate that the NEIMS assignment is divided into two phases i.e. Phase 1: Assessment, consultation and preparation of conceptual design for NEIMS and Phase 2: Development and commissioning of NEIMS.
This progress report presents the results and progress made during the implementation of Phase 1. The focus of this phase is on conducting a detailed landscape analysis to inform the conceptual design of the system. The main objectives the Phase 1 were to review relevant policy, legal, and regulatory frameworks map key energy sector stakeholders and institutions identify existing data sources, systems, and reporting mechanisms analyze national energy use patterns and highlight challenges and opportunities for integration.
The report indicate that the key findings of Phase 1 is that energy data in Tanzania is managed by multiple institutions with overlapping mandates and limited coordination. Traditional biomass fuels remain the dominant source of household energy, while petroleum products power transport and industry. Electricity access has grown, but disparities persist across urban and rural areas. Renewable energy, especially solar and wind, is expanding, though still underrepresented in national data systems. Existing data systems such as TANESCOs SCADA, EWURAs ERIS, and TPDCs PETREL are operational but fragmented and largely noninteroperable. There is limited use of international standards for data formatting or submission.
The report also identifies several challenges, including the absence of a dedicated regulation for data sharing, inadequate enforcement of reporting obligations, limited technical capacity, and poor integration between existing digital platforms. Moreover, data validation and analysis processes are inconsistent, often lacking automation or standardized procedures.
Despite these challenges, stakeholders have expressed strong support for NEIMS, recognizing its potential to improve energy planning, monitoring, and transparency. Recommendations arising from this phase include the need to:- - Clarify institutional mandates and designate NEIMS focal persons Develop standardized templates and data sharing protocols Align data collection with international frameworks such as IEA, IRENA, and UNSD. - Invest in a modular, cloud based system with GIS tools and real time dashboards - Build human and technical capacity across data supplying, processing and storing institutions - Establish legal and policy mechanisms to support system enforcement and sustainability.
Proposed NEIMS Conceptual Framework (System Ideation)
As part of this progress phase, a preliminary system ideation has been developed to guide the upcoming conceptual design of the NEIMS. This ideation serves as an initial visualization of how the system could be structured based on current data availability, stakeholder needs, and institutional capacities observed during this assignment. It is not a final system design, but rather a foundation for detailed architecture development in the next phase of the project. The ideation outlines the endtoend data lifecycle envisioned for NEIMS, structured into four key stages:
Inputs: Energy data will originate from a wide range of institutions, including MoE, NBS, TANESCO, EWURA, TPDC, PURA, REA, MNRT, MoA, and others.
The system will collect data on electricity, petroleum, biomass, natural gas, renewable energy, clean cooking, energy efficiency, and access. Inputs will arrive in various formatsExcel spreadsheets, hardcopy reports, APIs, dashboards on different reporting cycles (monthly, quarterly, annually). Integration: NEIMS will interface with both existing institutional systems (e.g., SCADA, LUKU, ERIS, TISIS etc) and manual input mechanisms (upload templates, forms). This stage will harmonize data formats, ensure consistency, and prepare the data for further analysis.
Processing: The system will apply both automated and manual validation processes to maintain data integrity. It will support key analytical functions such as national energy balances, disaggregation by source and sector, access and project tracking, GIS mapping, and alignment with SDG 7 indicators.
Outputs: The expected outputs include interactive dashboards, timeseries datasets, regional and national statistics, energy access maps, and policy reports. These will serve a wide range of stakeholders, including government ministries, regulators, development partners, private sector actors, academics &researchers and the general public.
This ideation emphasizes the need for data sustainability (embedding reporting into institutional processes), validation (automated and manual checks), accessibility (user friendly interfaces and formats), and alignment with global frameworks (e.g., IEA, IRENA, AFREC, UNSD, SDG 7). The proposed data flow structure is illustrated Annex 6 of the attached Narrative Report. This ideation will serve as a starting point for the detailed conceptual and system design phase to follow.
Remarks: The implementation of Phase 1 of the NEIMS development project is still ongoing but has made substantial progress toward establishing the groundwork for an integrated energy information management system in Tanzania. Through desk review and stakeholder consultations, this phase has identified key policies, legal frameworks, and institutional roles relevant to energy data. It has also provided a clearer picture of the current energy use patterns across different sources and sectors.
Preliminary findings show that although several institutions are involved in collecting and managing energy data, the landscape remains fragmented, with inconsistent formats, duplicated efforts, and a lack of formalized data sharing mechanisms. The engagement of stakeholders has been instrumental in highlighting existing capacities, data flows, and technical challenges. These insights are crucial for informing the systems conceptual design and guiding its technical and institutional architecture in subsequent phases.
Since the project has successfully completed Phase 1 of the NEIMS development, which involved reviewing relevant policy, legal, and regulatory frameworks mapping key energy sector stakeholders and institutions identifying existing data sources, systems, and reporting mechanisms analyzing national energy use patterns and highlighting challenges and opportunities for system integration.
As part of this phase, a preliminary system ideation has been developed to guide the forthcoming conceptual design of NEIMS. This ideation provides an initial visualization of how the system could be structured, informed by the current state of data availability, stakeholder needs, and institutional capacities observed during implementation. It is not a final system design but rather a foundation for developing the detailed system architecture in the next project phase.
Considering the above progress in the development of the National Energy Information Management System (NEIMS), the likelihood of achieving the project objectives by the end of the intervention given the current risk level remains high. The Embassy will continue to maintain close follow-up to further enhance the chances of full achievement of the intended objectives.
